Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.
data.title: Gym Hand & Pile: selection highlight raises with the card; raise slider max 180 / default 60

## Summary

Research spike to determine the client-side follow-detection mechanism for the "Follow us on Steam" incentive. The Steam client SDK has no direct "user follows this game's store page" call, so candidates must be verified before committing. This feature produces the decision-gate report that F4 depends on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A report documents and evaluates each candidate: `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(<developer account>)` (client-side, no backend), Steam Web API `IPlayerService` (game-page follow, needs server + publisher API key), and any other client-side candidates discovered.
- [ ] The report states a recommendation and flags the UX impact of each candidate (e.g. follows developer account vs game page).
- [ ] The recommendation is confirmed with the user (decision gate) and recorded in this item before F4 implementation commits to a mechanism.
- [ ] Any unknown (e.g. whether a server component is acceptable) is surfaced as an open question with options, not silently assumed.

## Minimal Implementation

- Prototype a minimal probe using the Steamworks SDK against a real Steam account (dev environment with Steam running).
- Research Steamworks SDK docs / community reports for `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing` semantics.
- Write findings to the work item as a structured report (markdown), including a decision recommendation.
- No production code committed in this feature.

## Prototype/Experiment

Success = a clear recommendation with evidence (docs/community/experiment) that the implementer can act on without re-research.

## Dependencies

- Parent blocked-by CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (Electron launcher) — launcher must exist to run Steamworks in-app.

## Deliverables

- Decision-gate report (in work item comments).
- Confirmed mechanism choice.

## Goal (user story)

As a developer of the competitive mode, I want the balancing AI's decision layer (`MainStreetAiStrategy` / `GreedyStrategy` / `scoreAction` / `MainStreetAiPlayer`) adapted to shared-street competitive semantics, so the opponent plays competently on a street it does not fully own.

## Context

The existing heuristics assume the AI owns the whole street:
- `scoreBusinessAction` / `scorePlayBusinessFromHandAction` value `(income + synergy) * horizon - cost` with no ownership concept.
- `aiPlanningHorizon` measures distance to the win threshold via `computeScore`, which sums a single player's coins + reputation.
- `enumerateLegalActions` includes staff actions (`hire-staff`, `peek-incident-deck`) — competitive mode makes staff player-only.

Parent: Main Street competitive mode epic (CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30). Depends on per-owner income routing (sibling) so scoring can evaluate against the acting player's own resources.

## Scope

- Ownership-aware scoring: evaluate income, synergy, and horizon against the **AI's own** resources/businesses and its own win threshold (using the per-player state model from the competitive state sibling).
- Staff exclusion: competitive-mode action enumeration drops staff actions from the AI's option space.
- Determinism via seeded RNG is preserved.

## Out of scope

- Opponent-aware *denial* reasoning (blocking the opponent's best slot, buying to deny) — intentionally deferred to a follow-up child.
- Endless continuation — deferred to a separate top-level issue.
- N-player Monte Carlo — covered by the Monte Carlo harness sibling; architecture is N-player-ready (PlayerRecord[] indexed by owner) but the initial harness validates head-to-head (1 human vs 1 AI).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** `scoreAction` and the per-type scoring helpers evaluate placement/upgrade/event value using only the acting player's resources and owned businesses, with the planning horizon computed from the acting player's own score vs. their win threshold.
- [ ] **AC2:** Competitive-mode legal-action enumeration excludes `hire-staff` and staff-skill actions (peek), while the single-player enumeration is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC3:** Deterministic: same seed + same strategy produces identical action sequences; verified by a dedicated deterministic replay test.
- [ ] **AC4:** All existing single-player AI tests (`ai-strategy.test.ts`, hint consistency, balance guardrails) still pass unchanged.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — Ownership-aware `scoreAction`/per-type helpers + competitive `enumerateLegalActions` variant (staff excluded); single-player paths unchanged.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-ai-strategy.test.ts` — Dedicated competitive AI tests (ownership-aware scoring, staff exclusion, determinism).

## Related Work

- Parent: CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30 — Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street
- Depends on: competitive state model + income/event routing siblings (per-player resources/score needed for ownership-aware horizon)
data.title: Competitive AI strategy: ownership-aware, staff-free scoring for shared-street play

# Review all tests — test-suite value audit with reproducible skill

## Summary

Review the entire (~476-file) test suite to evaluate whether each test actually tests something useful, classify every file against the documented low-value anti-pattern categories, produce a recommended removal/clean-up list, convert each recommendation into a child work item, and author a repo-local skill that makes the review process reproducible.

## Problem statement

The test suite has grown to ~476 `*.test.ts` files (~139k lines) — 364 unit, 112 browser, 12 E2E (incl. 6 tutorial-E2E parts), 4 smoke, plus balance/electron/scripts/replay groups — since the last full-suite cleanup (CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR removed 32 low-value files from a 344-file suite). Low-value tests (placeholder assertions, source-code-grep tests, self-referential simulations, duplicates of core coverage, type-level-only checks, zero-assertion browser tests) accumulate silently, adding maintenance cost and runtime without detecting real regressions. This item performs a fresh, reproducible audit of the whole suite and converts findings into actionable tracked work.

## Users

- **Producer / maintainers** — want a defensible, recorded basis for pruning the suite and assurance that kept tests add value.
- **AI agents / future reviewers** — need a codified, repeatable procedure so a re-audit (after more growth) is a skill invocation, not a from-scratch investigation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Entire-suite review completed.** Every `*.test.ts` file (all ~476, across unit/browser/E2E/smoke/balance/electron/scripts/replay) is reviewed and classified as `keep` / `remove` / `clean-up` against the anti-pattern categories reused from CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR: source-code-grep assertions, placeholder/tautological tests (`expect(true).toBe(true)`), self-referential simulations (zero production-code imports), duplicates of core coverage, type-level/structural-only tests, and zero-assertion browser tests. *Verification:* a complete classification table (file → category/decision) is present in the report, and the reviewed file count reconciles with the inventory snapshot recorded at implementation start.
- **Removal & clean-up list delivered.** A categorised list of proposed removals/clean-ups is produced as `docs/dev/test-suite-review.md` and summarised in the work-item description, each entry listing file path, line count, category, and rationale. *Verification:* the report exists, is committed, and its per-category counts reconcile with the classification table.
- **Recommendations tracked as child work items.** Each removal/clean-up recommendation is created as a child work item under CG-0MTCOPO8U001UW2Y, each with a clear goal + measurable ACs, e.g.:
  ```bash
  wl create --parent CG-0MTCOPO8U001UW2Y --issue-type task --priority low --stage idea \
    --title "Test review: remove <group>" --description "…" --json
  ```
  **No test file is deleted or modified by this item itself** — the children carry out the changes. *Verification:* `wl show CG-0MTCOPO8U001UW2Y --children --json` lists the recommendation items and the repo diff for this item contains no test deletions/edits (only report, skill, docs).
- **Reproducible skill authored.** A repo-local skill `/skill:test-review` is created at `.pi/skills/test-review/SKILL.md` (project skill conventions: front-matter `name` + `description`, markdown body, optional `scripts/`) codifying the methodology — anti-pattern categories, the exact discovery commands (grep/find patterns), classification steps, report format, and the child-work-item creation convention. *Verification:* the skill's documented procedure is exercised end-to-end during implementation to reproduce (a subset of) the audit on a clean checkout, and the skill is registered in docs.
- **Documentation updated.** All related documentation reflects the changes — the review process, report, and the new `test-review` skill referenced in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and/or `AGENTS.md`. *Verification:* docs committed in the same change; no stale references to reviewed/removed files remain.
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** (Release quality gate; `npm test -- --project unit` minimum before push — see AGENTS.md.) *Verification:* `npm test -- --project unit` is green at completion.

## Constraints

- Investigation scope is the **entire** suite (producer-confirmed); no area of the repo is exempt.
- This item is analysis + recommendation + skill authoring only — it must not itself remove or modify tests (producer-confirmed deliverable shape: create work items for recommendations).
- Reuse the anti-pattern categories and reporting style of CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR for continuity (producer-confirmed); this is a fresh pass over the grown suite, not a duplicate.
- Tests guarding historical regressions, documented precedents (e.g. the 2026-07-31 cleanup's reference list), and tests with explicit work-item linkage should be treated as `keep` unless evidence shows they no longer assert anything.
- UK English in all written output; work-item descriptions/comments in Markdown; ignore-rule compliance when scanning the repo.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Subjective classification risk (scope: whole review).** "Useful" is a judgement call. *Mitigation:* every classification carries an evidence line (file, lines, category, observed pattern); when evidence is ambiguous the file defaults to `keep` and is noted as `uncertain` rather than proposed for removal. Median, conservative posture — prefer a false negative to a false removal.
- **Risk of deleting a regression guard.** *Mitigation:* flagged removals are recommendations only and are executed by child work items through the normal implement → audit gate; a reviewer sees the full list before any deletion lands.
- **Browser/E2E static-review limits.** The 112 browser + 12 E2E files cannot be valued purely by static inspection. *Assumption:* classification there uses structure/assertion inspection and run-cost evidence; anything uncertain is `keep` with a `needs-manual-verification` note.
- **Scope-creep risk.** The review will surface adjacent opportunities (test-helper deduplication, fixture consolidation, runtime tuning). *Mitigation:* record these as separate linked work items (`discovered-from:CG-0MTCOPO8U001UW2Y`), never as additional scope inside this item.
- **Inventory drift.** The suite grew from 344 → 476 files between cleanups and will keep growing. *Assumption:* the reviewed snapshot is the commit at implementation start, and the report records that commit hash; the new skill is the mechanism for refreshing the audit later.
- **Skill-staleness risk.** A written procedure can drift from the suite it describes. *Mitigation:* the skill documents the discovery commands and the report format, and the report records inventory counts, so a re-run diffs cleanly.
- **Overlap risk with CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR.** *Mitigation:* the report treats the 2026-07-31 removals as already-handled and re-audits only what exists today; near-misses are compared against that item's taxonomy for consistency.

## Existing state

- 476 `*.test.ts` files (~139k lines) under `tests/` across unit/browser/E2E/smoke/balance/electron/scripts/replay groups (counts verified at intake, 2026-09-15).
- Prior full-suite cleanup: CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR (completed, 2026-07-31) removed 32 files (~3,806 lines) and stripped dead assertions from 8 kept files; its category list is the reference taxonomy for this audit.
- Preliminary find at intake: `tests/main-street/MainStreetApplicant.test.ts` (721 lines) contains 30 `expect(true).toBe(true)` placeholder branches behind a "function landed yet?" `require()` probe; the guarded functions (`resolveStaffApplicant`, `hireStaffApplicant`, `declineStaffApplicant`, `letGoStaffMember`) now exist in `MainStreetEngine.ts` (lines 3103–3203), so the guards are dead code and the `require` probe may be vacuous under Vitest ESM (`"type": "module"`). Prime removal/clean-up candidate to verify first.
- Repo-local skills precedent: `.pi/skills/release-windows/`, `.pi/skills/tce-game-dev/` (front-matter + markdown body + optional `scripts/`); documented in `docs/DEVELOPER.md`.

## Desired change

- A committed, versioned audit report (`docs/dev/test-suite-review.md`) that a future agent can re-run and diff against.
- A `test-review` skill that automates/codifies the re-audit so the entire process is reproducible on demand.
- Child work items (one per recommendation or recommendation group) that carry out the removals/clean-ups through the normal implement workflow.

## Commands (copy-paste ready)

```bash
# Inventory snapshot (record the commit + counts in the report)
git rev-parse HEAD
find tests -name '*.test.ts' -type f | wc -l

# Discovery probes used for classification
grep -rc 'expect(true)\.toBe(true)' tests --include='*.test.ts' | grep -v ':0'
grep -rl 'readFileSync' tests --include='*.test.ts'

# Quality gate before push
npm test -- --project unit && npm run build
```

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/test-suite-review.md` — the audit report (classification table + removal/clean-up list) — **new**
- `.pi/skills/test-review/SKILL.md` — the reproducible audit skill — **new** (optional `scripts/` helpers alongside)
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `AGENTS.md` — reference the report and skill — **edited**
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetApplicant.test.ts` — first confirmed candidate (clean-up/removal) — **touched by a child work item, not this item**
- `tests/**/*.test.ts` — the ~476 files reviewed (read-only here) — **reviewed**

## Related work

- **CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR** — Test suite cleanup: remove 32 low-value test files and strip dead assertions (completed; the taxonomy + precedent this audit extends).
- **CG-0MS9EJ3JT008ME4I** — Review testing patterns, CI/CD, and project infrastructure (completed).
- **CG-0MSZ4TN5Z001JADX** — Speed up browser tests and create test profiles (completed).
- **CG-0MSJ7ZXDB002CX97** — AGENTS.md: document when and how to run per-game, full-suite, and browser tests (completed).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Does 'all tests' mean the *entire* suite (including the 112 browser tests and 12 E2E/tutorial files), or should the review be limited to the fast unit project?" — Answer (producer): "entire suite". Source: interactive reply (2026-09-15).
- Q2: "Should this item deliver only a review artefact (removal list) with deletion deferred to a follow-up work item, or also execute removals here?" — Answer (producer): "create work items for recommendations". Interpretation: this item produces the report AND creates child work items carrying the removals; it does not itself delete/modify tests. Source: interactive reply (2026-09-15).
- Q3: "Reuse the anti-pattern categories from CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR? Confirm this is a fresh pass over the grown suite rather than a duplicate, and list any must-keep files/areas?" — Answer (producer): "confirmed". Interpretation: reuse the taxonomy; fresh pass over the ~476-file suite; no exempt areas. Source: interactive reply (2026-09-15).
- Q4 (new AC, added by producer): "Add a new AC which is to create a skill to make this process reproducible." — Answer (producer): directive to include AC4 (reproducible `test-review` skill). Source: interactive reply (2026-09-15).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MQHAR5AF002XPYI** – Tests for reusable undo/redo button mechanism (completed)
- **CG-0MTH7COKM0004FCJ** – [test-failure] <suite exited 1>: npm --silent test — failing test (completed)
- **CG-0MQSF0385003SXHV** – [test-failure] main-street-tutorial-e2e.browser.test.ts: resource exhaustion after repeated Phaser game create/destroy cycles (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: acceptance, actually, add, added, adding (+317 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, actually, add, added, adding (+248 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md` — matched: acs, actionable, actually, add, added (+229 more)

## Summary
Phaser camera zoom/pan for Main Street that reveals neighbouring streets on demand (always available, never gated). 1×1 at default zoom fits existing layout; zooming out reveals the surrounding street cells.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `MainStreetScene` owns a camera/zoom state (e.g. `zoomLevel` + `cameraOffset`) on `MainStreetState` or scene-local; wheel/pinch or +/- buttons change zoom, drag/arrow pans when zoomed out; interaction is always available (no milestone/turn gating).
2. At zoom 1× the viewport shows exactly the original 10-slot street with identical framing; at zoom 2× at least one ring of neighbouring streets is visible in-canvas with correct spacing/gaps.
3. Input hit-testing (slot click, drag-drop commerce placement, hand interactions) maps through the camera transform — placing a card on any visible street/slot works.
4. Reduced-motion preference respected for zoom animations; HUD chrome (market, hand, log, challenges) stays fixed while only the street canvas transforms.
5. `npm run build` green; `npx vitest run --project browser tests/main-street/camera-zoom.browser.test.ts` (or smoke equivalent) passes for 1× framing and 2× zoom reveal.

## Minimal Implementation
- Store `cameraZoom`/`cameraPan` on state or scene; wire Phaser Camera2D zoom/scroll or manual container scale+offset (choose the path that avoids breaking SLL layout — document decision).
- Add zoom controls (+/− buttons + wheel handler) via `MainStreetInputManager` / `MainStreetScene`.
- Update layout/renderer to compute visible street cells from viewport + zoom and set `streetContainer` transform accordingly.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: 2D street grid & adjacency resolver

## Deliverables
- Updated `MainStreetScene.ts`, `MainStreetInputManager.ts`, `MainStreetRenderer.ts` / `MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts` with camera/zoom

## Goal (user story)

As a developer, I want income to accrue only to the owning player of each placed business and shared events/incidents to retain their existing semantics routed per-owner, so the competitive economy is legible and testable.

## Context

`applyIncome` / adjacency income and `resolveEvent`/`resolveIncident` are single-player (one resourceBank/finalScore). Once street slots are owner-tagged (state-model sibling) and the phase machine delegates Income/Incident to per-owner handlers, the routing must be precise. Incident/Investment event regression risk: silent divergence where the wrong owner is credited or both are affected.

## Scope

- Per-owner income: each placed business's income (base + adjacency + upgrades + salary/ongoing) accrues only to its slot owner.
- Shared events/incidents: street-wide Investment events and incidents retain existing resolution semantics, routed per-owner as specified (design within planning: per-owner effects vs. shared board effects).
- Single-player (N=1) income path unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Phase machine / win condition (sibling).
- AI strategy / Monte Carlo.
- Endless continuation (deferred).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** Income for each placed business accrues only to the owning player (verified by per-owner fixtures covering base + synergy + upgrade + salary/ongoing).
- [ ] **AC2:** Shared Investment events and incidents retain existing resolution semantics and are routed per-owner as specified (design within planning); verified by per-owner event unit tests.
- [ ] **AC3:** Deterministic replay: same seed → identical per-owner income/event sequences.
- [ ] **AC4:** N=1 regression: income/event behaviour matches the pre-competitive single-player baseline.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Per-owner `applyIncome` variant, shared event/incident routing.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — Per-owner income computation helpers.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-income-events.test.ts` — Dedicated competitive income/event tests (per-owner fixtures, shared-event routing, determinism, N=1 regression).

## Related Work

- Parent: CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30
- Depends on: competitive state model (owner-tagged slots) + shared-day phase machine (closing-phase delegation)
- Required by: competitive AI strategy (CG-0MT5X3N79002S038 — ownership-aware scoring) + Monte Carlo harness

## Goal (user story)

As a developer/QA, I want a head-to-head Monte Carlo harness for competitive mode (extending MainStreetMonteCarlo) that runs ≥200 seeds and produces win/score distributions plus per-player metrics, so balance between player and AI can be measured across seeded runs.

## Context

`MainStreetMonteCarlo` is single-player only (`runMonteCarlo` / `runAllCombinations` with one strategy × one difficulty per run). Competitive mode needs head-to-head metrics: both players' win/score distributions plus per-player diagnostics. Architecture is N-player-ready (PlayerRecord[] indexed by owner), but the harness validates the head-to-head (human vs 1 AI) path initially; N>2 extension is a future parameterisation.

## Scope

- Head-to-head harness extending `MainStreetMonteCarlo` (new entry point or flag): both players act per shared-day, same seed → deterministic head-to-head run.
- ≥200 seeds; outputs win/score distributions plus per-player metrics (wins per owner, average score per owner, draw/early-end handling).
- Single-player AI tests (`ai-strategy.test.ts`, balance guardrails) still pass unchanged.

## Out of scope

- AI strategy itself (sibling).
- Per-owner income routing (sibling).
- Rendering / scene (AC5 child).
- Endless continuation (deferred).
- N>2 Monte Carlo — harness is N-player-extensible (numOpponents param) but AC4 validates head-to-head; broader N is a follow-up.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** Head-to-head harness runs ≥200 seeds with deterministic head-to-head execution (same seed → same per-owner outcome) and produces win/score distributions (win rate per owner, median/average score per owner).
- [ ] **AC2:** Per-player metrics include at least wins, average score, and loss-reason distribution per owner plus a deterministic summary (draw/early-end handling documented).
- [ ] **AC3:** Extension of `MainStreetMonteCarlo` (not a replacement); existing `runMonteCarlo` / `runAllCombinations` and `monte-carlo-balance.test.ts` still pass.
- [ ] **AC4:** Validated against the adapted competitive AI strategy (CG-0MT5X3N79002S038).

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Competitive head-to-head harness extension (win/score distributions, per-player metrics).
- `tests/main-street/competitive-monte-carlo.test.ts` — Dedicated competitive Monte Carlo tests (determinism, distributions, guardrails).

## Related Work

- Parent: CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30
- Depends on: competitive state model + phase machine + income routing + AI strategy (CG-0MT5X3N79002S038)
- Architecture: N-player-ready state/phase; harness parametrises head-to-head initially

## Goal (user story)

As a player, I want the shared street rendered with owner-coloured slots, shared-market phase alternation, and SFX/animations (per AGENTS.md §8), so competitive ownership is visually and audibly unambiguous.

## Context

AC5 of the parent epic is engine-only: no game-selector entry, no competitive scene, no competitive UI chrome. This planning-created child (per AC5 “deferred to a planning child” and producer Q2 “planning”) captures the deferred rendering scope for the next milestone. Worker must use core-engine animation helpers with `soundManager` + `sfx` (AGENTS.md §8: every animated action needs sound + animation; SFX keys via `COMMON_SFX_KEYS`, no literals).

## Scope

- Competitive scene (Phaser scene) with SLL layout.
- Owner-coloured street: each placed business's street slot tinted by owner (e.g. player = blue, AI = red) so the shared grid's ownership is immediately readable.
- Shared-market phase alternation: alternate MarketPhases within a shared day with visible whose-turn affordance.
- SFX/animations for all competitive actions (deal/flip/place/discard/illegal) via helpers + `SoundManager`, respecting reduced-motion and mute.
- Turn alternation SFX/animation sequencing so AI actions are visible (delayed AI turn like Coloretto precedent).

## Out of scope

- Engine state/phase/income/AI/Monte Carlo (parent epic siblings).
- Game-selector entry — include only when the scene is ready for play (within this child).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** Competitive scene renders the shared street with per-slot owner colour (player vs AI unambiguously distinct); SLL layout used (no hardcoded pixel positions).

# Audit report — classify all ~499 test files

## Goal
Run a comprehensive review of every `*.test.ts` file in the suite (499 files at commit f601fb4, ~145k lines), classify each against the anti-pattern taxonomy, produce `docs/dev/test-suite-review.md`, and create child work items for each removal/clean-up group.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. **Complete classification table** — Every file is classified as `keep` / `remove` / `clean-up` with evidence (file path, line count, category, observed pattern, rationale).
2. **Inventory reconciles** — The report's per-category counts sum to the total file count (499 at audit commit). The report records the audit commit hash.
3. **Removal/clean-up list** — Each proposed removal has file path, line count, category, and rationale.
4. **Report committed** — `docs/dev/test-suite-review.md` exists in the repo diff.
5. **Removal recommendation children created** — For each removal/clean-up group, create a child work item under CG-0MTCOPO8U001UW2Y with `wl create --parent CG-0MTCOPO8U001UW2Y --issue-type task --priority low --stage idea --title "Test review: remove <group>" --description "…" --json`. Each child has a clear goal + measurable ACs. **No test file is deleted by this child — only recommendations are created.**

## Anti-pattern taxonomy (from CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR)
- **source-code-grep**: assert the text of source files (readFileSync + toContain/string index on .ts files), break on any refactor, never detect behavioral regressions
- **placeholder/tautological**: `expect(true).toBe(true)` with no real assertion
- **self-referential simulations**: import zero production code, test only their own structure
- **duplicates of core coverage**: test something already tested by a deeper core-engine test
- **type-level/structural-only**: assert factory returns N fields the compiler already enforces
- **zero-assertion browser tests**: browser tests with no `expect()` calls

## Known candidates (pre-scan)
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetApplicant.test.ts` (721 lines, 30 expect(true).toBe(true) placeholder branches — functions now exist, guards may be dead code)
- `tests/helpers/main-street-tutorial-cleanup.browser.test.ts` (1 expect(true).toBe(true) defensive guard)
- `tests/core-engine/ChallengeSystem.test.ts` — source-grep on ChallengeSystem.ts
- `tests/core-engine/SaveLoad.test.ts` — source-grep on SaveLoad.ts
- `tests/core-engine/DifficultyPresets.test.ts` — source-grep on DifficultyPresets.ts
- `tests/core-engine/no-runtime-synthesis.test.ts` — reads .ts source files

## Notes
- Asset integrity tests (readFileSync on JSON manifests, SVG icons) are NOT source-grep — they verify data files, not source code. Keep these.
- Browser tests that boot Phaser scenes and check rendered elements are genuine UI tests.
- When in doubt, classify as `keep` with a `needs-manual-verification` note.
- Removal children are created as siblings of this child, under CG-0MTCOPO8U001UW2Y.
